task: Design MIMO antenna for microwave-based brain imaging stroke detection
key_results: T-shaped two-port antenna operates 3.1–6 GHz with ECC <0.005, diversity gain >9.9 dB, mutual coupling <−15 dB in head model
comments: Strong isolation and MIMO metrics support the application, but actual stroke detection performance (sensitivity/specificity) is not quantified in the abstract.

title: Design of a slotted bowtie dual-polarized antenna for Sub-6 GHz multi-service wireless applications
task: Design dual-band dual-polarized antenna for sub-6 GHz wireless
key_results: Operates at 2.52 GHz and 4.42 GHz with 220 MHz and 420 MHz bandwidths; achieves 40 dB port isolation and peak gain of 7.6 dBi
comments: Practical design with reflector optimization, but dual-band separation suggests two somewhat independent resonances rather than true wideband operation.

title: Accurate alpha-particle stopping power measurements in graphenic carbon foils and their application to high-precision, non-destructive areal density determination
task: Non-destructive areal density determination of graphenic carbon foils via alpha-particle stopping power
key_results: Alpha spectroscopy yields <1% relative uncertainty; mean excitation energies (73±2) eV and (85±3) eV for KETEK and Applied Nanotech foils respectively; stopping-power model validated across 5.0–5.8 MeV
comments: High-precision metrology well-suited for thin foils, but applicability limited by angular straggling beyond thin-target approximation; model-dependent composition interpretation requires independent validation.

model_io.model: Three-isotope mixed alpha source with high-resolution spectroscopy
inputs: graphenic carbon foils (KETEK and Applied Nanotech)

model_io.model: Modified Bethe formalism with Barkas and Bloch corrections

hypotheses.hypothesis: Modified Bethe formalism with empirically adjusted mean excitation energy best describes stopping power across 5.0–5.8 MeV
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: provides most consistent description; systematic differences between foils consistent with composition and microstructure
